{{Short description|1989 single by Mantronix}} {{EngvarB|date=July 2014}} {{Use mdy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox song | name = Got to Have Your Love | cover = Mantronix Got to Have Your Love.jpg | alt = | type = single | artist = [[Mantronix]] featuring [[Wondress Hutchinson|Wondress]] | album = [[This Should Move Ya]] | released = {{start date|1989|12}} | recorded = | studio = | venue = | genre = {{hlist|[[Electro music|Electro]]-[[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]|[[hip house]]}} | length = 8:21 | label = [[Capitol Records|Capitol]] | writer = * [[Bryce Wilson|Bryce "Luvah" Wilson]] * [[Kurtis Mantronik|Kurtis el Khaleel]] * Johnny D. Rodriguez | producer = Mantronix | chronology = [[Mantronix]] | prev_title = Join Me Please | prev_year = 1988 | next_title = Take Your Time | next_year = 1990 | misc = {{External music video|{{YouTube|7z_dNHwlBzM|"Got to Have Your Love"}}}} }} "'''Got to Have Your Love'''" is a song by American [[hip hop]] and [[Electro (music)|electro funk]] group [[Mantronix]], featuring vocals from American recording artist [[Wondress Hutchinson|Wondress]]. It was released by [[Capitol Records]] in December 1989 as the lead single from Mantronix's fourth studio album, ''[[This Should Move Ya]]'' (1990). The song is written by band members [[Bryce Wilson]] and [[Kurtis Mantronik]] along with Johnny D. Rodriguez, and produced by Mantronix. It reached number four in the UK, number seven in Finland and number eight in Ireland. It is recognized as the group's [[signature song]]. ==Song information== "Got to Have Your Love" was written by Mantronix members [[Bryce Wilson]] and [[Kurtis Mantronik]], alongside Johnny D. Rodriguez. Mantronik stated that "When I did 'Got to Have Your Love', I did it for a reason. I did it because I wanted to get a song on the radio."{{cite web|url=http://www.cheebadesign.com/legends/articleE.html|title=Messin' with Mantronix|publisher=cheebadesign.com|access-date=September 8, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061102113745/http://www.cheebadesign.com/legends/articleE.html|archive-date=November 2, 2006}} ==Critical reception== Upon the release, Bill Coleman from ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' wrote that the act "is back on the right track with an [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]-textured [[Hip hop music|hip-hop]] track (à la vintage [[Joyce Sims]]) sporting a sensuous vocal performance by newcomer [[Wondress Hutchinson|Wondress]]. Black radio needs to be on this tip as well."{{cite magazine|first=Bill|last=Coleman|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/80s/1989/BB-1989-12-09.pdf|title=Single Reviews|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=December 9, 1989|page=73|access-date=September 26, 2020}} Dave Obee from ''[[Calgary Herald]]'' complimented the group for "find[ing] a funky groove".Obee, Dave (February 8, 1990). "Recent Releases". ''[[Calgary Herald]]''. Push from ''[[Melody Maker]]'' felt they "returns with what is basically a half-hearted [[hip-house]] thang", calling it "slappy, slushy and slumped at the waist."{{cite magazine|author=Push|work=[[Melody Maker]]|title=Singles|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/52014187340/|date=January 6, 1990|access-date=February 24, 2023}} Pan-European magazine ''[[Music & Media]]'' named it "attractive hip/house featuring a melodic and soulful lead vocal by Wondress. Classy stuff."{{cite magazine|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1990/MM-1990-01-20.pdf|title=Previews: Singles|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=7|issue=3|date=January 20, 1990|page=20|access-date=February 22, 2018}} David Giles from ''[[Music Week]]'' remarked that Mantronik "appears to have stepped into [[Soul II Soul]]/[[Inner City (band)|Inner City]] domain, roping in a bluesy female vocalist and coating her in swooming strings (sampled naturally). Altogether a funker effort than those of his UK counterparts".{{cite magazine|first= David |last= Giles |title= Singles |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= January 6, 1990 |page= 19 |access-date= October 29, 2020 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1990/MW-1990-01-06.pdf}} Jack Barron from ''[[New Musical Express|NME]]'' wrote, "Curtis has obviously been listening to Soul II Soul over there in [[New York City|New York]] and here compresses together a woman singer called Wondress (what a groovy name) and a rapper on an organic shuffle. Not instantaneous, but I've got a feeling 'Got to Have Your Love' is one of those records which will creep up on you like infatuation as opposed to some pug ugly swine with an axe in its trotter."{{cite magazine|first=Jack|last=Barron|work=[[New Musical Express|NME]]|title=Singles|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/nothingelseon/51862222193/|date=December 16, 1989|access-date=February 24, 2023}} [[Miranda Sawyer]] from ''[[Smash Hits]]'' praised it as "perfection".{{cite magazine|first=Miranda|last=Sawyer|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/smashhits90s/41799631650/in/album-72157669443828447/|title=Review: LPs|magazine=[[Smash Hits]]|issue=321|page=44|date=March 20, 1991|access-date=March 8, 2020|author-link=Miranda Sawyer}} ==Retrospective response== In his retrospective review of the ''[[This Should Move Ya]]'' album, Ron Wynn from [[AllMusic]] described "Got to Have Your Love" as a "strong single".{{cite web|first= Ron |last= Wynn |title= Mantronix – ''This Should Move Ya'' |publisher= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= November 4, 2020 |url= https://www.allmusic.com/album/this-should-move-ya-mw0000206263}} While reviewing the compilation album ''The Best Of: 1985-1999'', Andy Crysell from ''[[NME]]'' stated that the song "remains a bewitching [[Soul music|soul]] classic".{{cite web|first= Andy |last= Crysell |title= Mantronix / Kurtis Mantronik – The Best Of: 1985-1999 / I Sing The Body Electro |url= http://www.nme.com/reviews/reviews/19990301115604reviews.html |work= [[NME]] |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20000817192508/http://www.nme.com/reviews/reviews/19990301115604reviews.html |access-date= November 24, 2020|archive-date= August 17, 2000 }} In 2020, ''[[Mixmag]]'' included "Got to Have Your Love" in their list of "The Best Basslines in Dance Music", writing, "Sublime, soul-licked vocals from Wondress definitely gave it the flavour it needed for mainstream success, but it's also charged by one of the best basslines in pop history."{{cite web|url=https://mixmag.net/feature/best-basslines-dance-music|title=The Best Basslines In Dance Music, According To You|magazine=[[Mixmag]]|date=May 7, 2020|access-date=October 16, 2024}} ==Music video== The accompanying music video for "Got to Have Your Love" includes a cameo by former child model and now music producer [[Felix Howard]].{{Cite web|last=Dazed|date=August 24, Rodriguez | producer = Rod Gammons | prev_title = [[Just a Little (Liberty X song)|Just a Little]] | prev_year = 2002 | next_title = [[Holding On for You]] | next_year = 2002 | misc = {{External music video|{{YouTube|AhBkW-t4NfM|"Got to Have Your Love"}}}} }} In 2002, English-Irish music group [[Liberty X]] recorded "Got to Have Your Love" for their debut studio album, ''[[Thinking It Over (album)|Thinking It Over]]'' (2002). It was one of three tracks to be recorded for the British version of the album, as it did not feature on the original edition, ''To Those Who Wait''. The song was released on September 9, 2002, as the fourth single from the album and reached number two on the [[UK Singles Chart]].{{cite news|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/2260108.stm|title=Double top for Atomic Kitten|publisher=BBC News|date=September 15, 2002|access-date=November 8, 2021}} It also charted at number eight in Ireland and number 12 in the Netherlands. ===Music video=== The song's accompanying music video was filmed at Silent Waters in [[Montego Bay]], [[Jamaica]].
